coverage.rationale: The release plan defines rollout but no rollback compatibility check.
The approved data review covers the changed fields.

questions.question: Can the prior checkout version safely consume events emitted by the new version during rollback?
questions.omission_reason: The plan validates forward rollout only.
questions.importance: An incompatible rollback could duplicate or lose orders.
questions.ranking_rationale: High blast radius, low reversibility after mixed-version events, and the release gate is imminent.
questions.consequence: Rollback may corrupt order state or require manual reconciliation.
questions.blocking_rationale: Release approval depends on a demonstrated compatible rollback or a different rollout strategy.
questions.expected_answer_form: compatible with evidence, incompatible with mitigation, or rollout must change
questions.next_action: Run mixed-version contract tests and update the rollback plan.
assumptions: Both versions may run concurrently during rollback.
unknowns: Whether all consumers ignore the new optional field.
questions.monitoring: Track event rejection and order reconciliation metrics during rollout.
questions.reopen_trigger: Any consumer schema or deployment-order change.
disconfirming_evidence: A proven atomic cutover would reduce mixed-version risk.

questions.question: Which order-reconciliation threshold should trigger automatic rollback?
questions.omission_reason: Metrics are listed, but no decision threshold is assigned.
questions.importance: Without a threshold, operators may react inconsistently during a fast-moving release.
questions.ranking_rationale: Material operational impact and high time sensitivity, but recovery remains possible.
questions.consequence: Delayed rollback could expand customer impact.
questions.blocking_rationale: The team may proceed with a temporary conservative threshold if the owner accepts it.
questions.next_action: Record the threshold in the runbook and alert configuration.
assumptions: The reconciliation metric is available within five minutes.
unknowns: Normal peak variance after the schema change.
questions.monitoring: Compare reconciliation variance to the temporary threshold every five minutes.
questions.reopen_trigger: Observed variance exceeds the temporary threshold or monitoring latency changes.
